name: Refrigerant gases
description: Refrigerant gas for AC, chiller and refrigeration systems, from leading brands.
long_description: Every cooling system is built for one refrigerant, and topping up or recharging with the right gas, in the right amount, keeps it efficient and safe. We supply sealed cylinders of the common AC and refrigeration gases from established makers such as SRF (Floron), Gujarat Fluorochemicals, Navin Fluorine (Mafron), Honeywell (Genetron, Solstice), Chemours (Freon, Opteon) and Arkema (Forane).
match_by: The refrigerant on your unit's nameplate

parts.name: R32
parts.detail: Lower-GWP refrigerant used in most new inverter split ACs.
notes: Mildly flammable: use R32-rated tools, a vacuum pump suited to A2L gases, and good ventilation
Never top up an R22 or R410A unit with R32

parts.name: R410A
parts.detail: High-pressure HFC blend for split, ductable and VRF systems.
notes: Runs at about 1.6 times the pressure of R22: use R410A-rated gauges and hoses
Charge as liquid so the blend stays in the right proportions

parts.name: R22
parts.detail: HCFC used in older ACs; being phased out, for servicing existing units.
notes: Being phased out under the Montreal Protocol because it harms the ozone layer; supplied for servicing existing systems
When a major repair is due, ask us about replacing the unit with an R32 or R410A system

parts.name: R407C
parts.detail: Non-ozone-depleting blend used in place of R22 in package units and chillers.
parts.chemical_name: Blend of R32, R125 and R134a
notes: High temperature glide: always charge as liquid, and recharge fully after a leak rather than topping up
Retrofitting an R22 system needs an oil change to POE

parts.name: R134a
parts.detail: Medium-pressure HFC for chillers, car ACs and water coolers.
notes: Lower operating pressure than R22 or R410A
Car ACs need PAG oil; stationary systems use POE

parts.name: R404A
parts.detail: Blend for low and medium temperature refrigeration and cold rooms.
parts.chemical_name: Blend of R125, R143a and R134a
notes: Very high GWP: lower-GWP alternatives are being adopted for new refrigeration equipment
Charge as liquid

parts.name: R507A
parts.detail: Azeotropic blend for low temperature cold storage and freezers.
notes: Behaves like a single gas, so small top-ups do not shift the blend
Often used interchangeably with R404A in low temperature systems; check the compressor's approval first

parts.name: R454B
parts.detail: Lower-GWP replacement for R410A in new ductable and package units.
notes: Only for equipment designed for R454B; it is not a drop-in for R410A systems
Mildly flammable: use A2L-rated tools and good ventilation

parts.name: R290 (propane)
parts.detail: Natural hydrocarbon refrigerant with very low GWP.
parts.oil: As specified by the compressor maker (mineral, POE or PAO)
applications: Energy-efficient split ACs designed for R290
notes: Highly flammable: only for equipment built for R290, handled by trained technicians
Never use LPG cooking gas as a substitute; refrigerant grade is purified and dried

parts.name: R600a (isobutane)
parts.detail: Hydrocarbon refrigerant used in most modern domestic refrigerators.
parts.charging: By weight, with very small charges (grams)
notes: Highly flammable: only for appliances built for R600a
Charges are small, so use an accurate scale

parts.name: R1234yf
parts.detail: Ultra-low-GWP HFO replacing R134a in new car ACs.
parts.oil: PAG (as specified by the vehicle maker)
notes: Only for systems designed for R1234yf; car AC service ports differ from R134a
Mildly flammable: use A2L-rated equipment

signs: AC runs but cooling is weak
Ice forming on the indoor coil or pipes
Hissing sound or oily marks at joints (possible leak)
